text:
marta: Heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak we pushed yesterday we're seeing token misalignment on a subset of long-context requests. Outputs have shifted by a few tokens and some cached KV pages look stale.
ryan: ugh. Is this the kernel switch to the new attention tile?
marta: yeah, landed commit c7a3f0 -> changed kernel for 2048+ sequences. Repro on prod at ~10:42UTC, affected 0.6% of requests but they blow up for long contexts.
sam: logs? any request ids we can grep?
marta: pasted snippet from one trace: 
```
2026-03-18T10:42:12Z request_id=req_28a2 kv_page_id=page_118 expected_offset=4096 observed_start=4099
kv_block_tag=0x7f stale=true reuse_count=1
```
This shows the page start moved +3 tokens vs expected.
ryan: that looks like an alignment delta. Could be an off-by-one in append after eviction compaction.
lia: also check batching heuristics — if batching split changed, the KV append might be using a different base sequence length. Did batching window shrink?
alex: we profiled a repro run. Flamegraph attached (link: https://perf.redwood/snap/303401). The hotspot is kv::apply_delta during rollback.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy finished for canary/runtime-kernel v2.3.4 (c7a3f0) :thumbsup:
ryan: can we reproduce locally with long-context regression harness? I can try a bisect between c5b and c7a.
marta: repro steps I used: long prompt ~12k tokens, enable prefix caching, run 8 concurrent requests with varying seq lengths. Repro rate ~30% with those conditions.
sam: I also saw memory growth across sessions — long-lived worker's RSS creeps over 12h. Might be stale KV blocks never evicted.
lia: possible race between eviction thread and append path. If an eviction marks a page tombstone but a concurrent append reuses slot without updating tag, you get cross-request contamination.
alex: here's a small snippet I pulled from runtime debug: 
```
// simplified
if (!page->locked) {
  append_to_page(page, entry);
} else {
  // evicted -> move to free list
  move_page_out(page);
}
// missing atomic tag bump -> old consumer can still read
```
That missing atomic update would explain observed stale reads.
ryan: sounds like we need a quick guard: make append check the page epoch/tag and refuse if evicted, returning E_RETRY. Cheap fix while we bisect.
marta: I'll open a patch PR with guard + extra asserts and a regression test that runs the long-context harness with forced eviction frequency.
lia: also add metrics: per-page tag version and per-request observed-offset histogram so we can spot token drift.
sam: for immediate mitigation, can we enable stricter batching boundaries (disable batch coalescing for 2048+)? That reduces concurrency and might avoid the race.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0467 — KV-tag drift & stale-page reads affecting long-context responses.
alex: re: kernel selection, it may be indirectly exposing the timing window because the new kernel reduces per-token latency, increasing append/evict interleavings. We should include a test that simulates faster kernels.
ryan: agreed. Add a CI job that runs append/evict stress with artificially shortened kernel delays.
marta: PR: https://git.redwood/pr/8721 — guard + test + metric. Kickoff review?
lia: reviewing now. If green, let's rollback canary and apply guard to prod immediately.
sam: I'll prepare a short retro once we have root cause. For postmortem: include kernel timing sensitivity, batching heuristics, and KV tag invariants.
marta: thanks all — will post updates in this thread after the patch lands. :thumbsup:
